# [Baseline] - IOS - D - Software Updates

Enforces the latest iOS version on enrolled iPhones and iPads no later than 14 days after release (installation at 02:00), locks automatic download and installation of OS and security updates to on, and prevents the user from rolling back security improvements.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | iOS/iPadOS |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog |
| Assignment | — |
| checkId | `INTUNE-BASE-192-IOSDSoftwareUpdates` |
| Source | UniFy iOS/iPadOS Baseline v1.2 — SC - DEV - Software Update - Corporate Devices (CIS Apple iOS/iPadOS 26 Benchmark v1.0.0), compared with IntuneAdmin Apple iOS Benchmarks (Enforce Latest Software Update Version, Recommendation Cadence, Rapid Security Response); deferral period deliberately omitted |
| File | [`Baseline_IOS_D_Software_Updates.json`](Baseline_IOS_D_Software_Updates.json) |

> Mind the option numbers: for the automatic actions `_0` is Allowed (the user chooses) and `_1` is AlwaysOn — `_1` here, the same mistake that was fixed in MAC - D - Software Updates. For enforce latest, `_0` is in fact the only option (True). Deviations from UniFy: no deferral (combinedperiodindays 14) — with a deferral plus a 14-day deadline, a security update only appears on the day it is enforced; without a deferral the user can install it right away and day 14 is the safety net. Beta enrollment not set: the definition is called 'Program Enrollment (Unsupported)'. Rollback of Background Security Improvements is off (UniFy, CIS), unlike MAC - D - Software Updates where it is on. Recommended version set to Newest, same as IntuneAdmin. Compliance Device Health remains the access threshold with osMinimumVersion; this policy makes sure devices stay well above it.
